name: @yichus/api-mcp

tools.name: api_tools
tools.description: List the specialist tool families this server offers beyond the core tools, or open one. With no arguments it returns the core tool names and each family's name, one-line summary and tool names. With family it returns that family's tools with their descriptions and input schemas, and an MCP server that lists only the core tools adds them to its tool list. Any catalog tool can be called by name whether or not it is listed.

family.description: Optional family name from the no-argument answer, such as access or proofs. Omit to list the families.

tools.name: api_guide
tools.description: Return the pre-written agent guide for building a Bosatsu API with checked access rules. Call this first. Deterministic documentation; no model-generated advice. With no arguments it returns the table of contents, each section's title with one line on what it covers; with section it returns the full text of the sections whose title contains that text (case-insensitive) and, on no match, the list of titles; with full true it returns every section (full is ignored when section is given).

section.description: Optional title, or part of one: the full text of the matching sections is returned. Omit for the table of contents.

full.description: Optional; true returns the full text of every section (about 100k characters).

tools.name: api_scaffold
tools.description: Generate a Yichus-first Bosatsu API module: structs, Yichus/Access rules, owner-scoped or public handlers, and a Yichus/Service routing table, plus a matching Yichus/Frontend::FrontendSpec (frontendSource) for api_frontend. The result compiles and verifies; edit it, then api_verify.

package_name.description: Bosatsu package, PascalCase segments separated by slashes, e.g. My/Notes/Api

resources.description: JSON array of {name, fields:[{name,type}], policy}. type is String, Int, or Bool. policy is owner or public.

tools.name: api_verify
tools.description: Rerun the available safety checks from the typed IR of the given Bosatsu sources. Reports which properties still hold after edits. Topology is an input: undeclared defaults to multi-instance, where RMW and interleaving findings are violations. When the sources declare a Yichus/Organize AbstractionSpec or GroupSpec, the declared-structure property checks every declared claim the way api_organize's abstractions and layers lenses do: proven when all converge, violated when any declared claim diverges (a generator that does not hold its declared guard responsibility, a member that does not use its generator, or a package that uses a group its GroupSpec does not allow; the claim is named with its location), blocked when a declared generator, member, concept or package is absent or the declarations cannot be evaluated, and a warning when a GroupSpec allows a use the code never makes. Sources with no such declaration get no declared-structure property. operation-coverage checks that the storage checks saw every table operation in the program's own code: blocked names each one they did not (no site was extracted for it, its table is not a literal name or a top-level stored_table value, the primitive is passed or bound as a value instead of called, or it runs inside a helper or a closure a helper returns, where no read-then-write check pairs it with the caller's reads), and rmw-transactions and integrity block with it. Fix one by calling the primitive where it runs, in the handler or the transaction plan, on a table named by a literal or a top-level stored_table value. A warning means the program performs no storage operations. Warnings do not make proven false unless block_on_warnings lists them. Do not deploy unless proven is true.

sources.description: JSON array of {fileName, source} Bosatsu files for the API module.

instances.description: Deployment topology: 1 for a single engine instance, many (default) for multiple instances sharing one DB.

block_on_warnings.description: Optional JSON array of property ids (for example ["rmw-transactions", "integrity"]) or ["all"]. An id must name a property this verdict has; declared-structure exists only when the sources declare a spec; use all to block every warning whatever the program declares. A listed property whose status is warning makes proven false, as a violation would; its own status stays warning, and the verdict's blockedWarnings field names it. An id that names no property of this verdict is refused (ok false, errorKind invalid-arguments). Left out, warnings do not block.

tools.name: api_compile
tools.description: Parse and type-check Bosatsu API sources in memory (CompileKernel). No filesystem.

sources.description: JSON array of {fileName, source} Bosatsu files.

tools.name: api_report
tools.description: Build the program-report-2.0 map from the typed IR for whatever style of program the sources are (CRUD, flow, dist, escrow, unrouted IO). overview.surfaces names the present IR surfaces; needed names missing declarations with snippets. Pass format html for a self-contained HTML document.

protocol_case.description: Optional protocol-case-1.0 JSON; attaches a separate bounded protocol verdict without changing universal proof claims.

sources.description: JSON array of {fileName, source} Bosatsu files for the module.

instances.description: Deployment topology: 1 for a single engine instance, many (default) for multiple instances sharing one DB.

format.description: json (default) for the raw report, html for a self-contained HTML document.

title.description: Optional title for the HTML document.

detail.description: summary (default) keeps shape to per-package counts plus the IO/notable bindings; full enumerates every binding.

tools.name: api_add_artifact
tools.description: Return a paste-ready Bosatsu snippet for a report artifact (AccessSpec, ServiceDef, DistSpec, EscrowSpec, FlowSpec, Spec, FrontendSpec). Pass kind. Pass the same sources as api_report to fill names from the IR, or omit sources for a generic template. If the kind does not apply to those sources, the tool says so instead of emitting a misleading snippet.

kind.description: access, service, dist, escrow, flow, spec, or frontend

sources.description: Optional JSON array of {fileName, source}. When present, the snippet is filled from the typed IR.

resource.description: Optional table or cell name for generic access/escrow/spec templates.

policy.description: owner or public. Used for generic access templates.

name.description: Optional binding/service name for generic templates.

tools.name: api_law_check
tools.description: Check declared Yichus/Law obligations. Mode sampled (default) uses seeded generation: holds is bounded observation, never proof. Mode exhaustive checks every value of an accepted finite type or every distinct value of a Bosatsu FiniteObligation list; holds-exhaustive says every value of the type held, and holds-on-listed says only the listed values were checked. Unsupported domains, exceeded limits, unfinished witnesses, and worker failures never become a pass. Violated and inconclusive both mean not done. When the program declares routes, reach lists, for each law whose check it could read, the routes that reach what that check calls; a law listed with no routes is one no route of the service calls, and a law left out of reach was not compared.

sources.description: JSON array of {fileName, source} Bosatsu files including the Obligation bindings.

module_name.description: Optional module name for the verdict artifact (default Laws).

seed.description: Optional run seed; the whole run replays from this one number (default 41).

mode.description: sampled (default) or exhaustive; exhaustive never falls back to a seeded pass.

maximum.description: Maximum finite inputs per obligation in exhaustive mode (default 256, hard cap 4096).

tools.name: api_why
tools.description: Evaluate ONE binding on concrete typed inputs and report why the output is what it is. Pick the binding from a diagram or report by its Pkg/Name::binding id. Provide inputs as JSON (missing ones are seeded deterministically); the tool returns the typed inputs and output with named rendering, soundFacts (static dataflow: per-parameter influence that holds for EVERY input), and observed (bounded seeded runs: touched bindings, per-parameter and per-field vary-one-fix-rest differentials). soundFacts and observed are disjoint on purpose: an observed-constant result is NOT independence, and every observed sentence says 'bounded observation, not proof'. IO handlers run against a fresh in-memory world (optionally seeded via rows) and report the table rows after the run; handler differentials rebuild the world from the same seeded rows for every variation (a varied principal's roles against fixed rows flips a gated route).

sources.description: JSON array of {fileName, source} Bosatsu files for the module.

binding.description: The binding to evaluate, as Pkg/Name::binding (the id shown on diagrams and reports).

inputs.description: Optional JSON object {param: value} of provided inputs. Values use the same JSON encoding api types use; a nullary enum constructor is written {"Ctor": {}} (the form the tool prints), and the bare object of a constructor's fields is read too. Unlisted params are seeded from the seed.

seed.description: Optional run seed; the whole run replays byte-identically from this one number (default 41).

observe.description: Optional; false skips the differential runs and returns only the evaluation plus soundFacts (default true).

rows.description: Optional JSON object {table: [row, ...]} seeding the in-memory world for an IO handler run.

instructions: This server lists its core tools first. The specialist families are ship, access, concurrency, proofs, orientation and changes. Call api_tools to see each family's summary and tool names, and api_tools with family set to one of those names to open it: its tools join the list. Any tool runs by name either way.
